events.title: Amsterdam is first mentioned in a charter
events.description: Count Floris V of Holland granted toll exemption to the people living near the dam on the Amstel. The charter is the earliest document to mention Amsterdam, then a small fishing settlement.
events.html: Count Floris V of Holland granted toll exemption to the people living near the dam on the Amstel. The charter is the earliest document to mention Amsterdam, then a small fishing settlement.

events.title: Michael Servetus is burned for heresy in Geneva
events.description: Geneva's council, with John Calvin's backing, had the Spanish physician and theologian Michael Servetus burned for denying the Trinity. His death became a landmark in arguments for religious toleration.
events.html: Geneva's council, with John Calvin's backing, had the Spanish physician and theologian Michael Servetus burned for denying the Trinity. His death became a landmark in arguments for religious toleration.

events.title: A Dutch army retakes Grave from the French
events.description: After a siege begun on 25 July, the French garrison surrendered the fortress town of Grave, in what is now North Brabant, to a Dutch army. The French had held the town since an army under Turenne forced its surrender in 1672.

events.title: William Penn arrives to found Pennsylvania
events.description: William Penn reached the Delaware River aboard the Welcome to take possession of his new colony. He laid out Philadelphia as a planned 'greene Countrie Towne' that later hosted the Declaration of Independence.
events.html: William Penn reached the Delaware River aboard the Welcome to take possession of his new colony. He laid out Philadelphia as a planned 'greene Countrie Towne' that later hosted the Declaration of Independence.

events.title: The first Federalist essay is published
events.description: Writing as 'Publius', Alexander Hamilton published the first of 85 essays urging New Yorkers to ratify the new US Constitution. With Madison and Jay he produced the most influential commentary on the Constitution.
events.html: Writing as 'Publius', Alexander Hamilton published the first of 85 essays urging New Yorkers to ratify the new US Constitution. With Madison and Jay he produced the most influential commentary on the Constitution.

events.title: Napoleon enters Berlin after the Prussian defeat at Jena–Auerstedt
events.description: Emperor Napoleon entered Berlin without a fight, three days after French forces had captured the Prussian capital following their victory at Jena–Auerstedt. From the city he later issued the Berlin Decree implementing his Continental System.
events.html: Emperor Napoleon entered Berlin without a fight, three days after French forces had captured the Prussian capital following their victory at Jena–Auerstedt. From the city he later issued the Berlin Decree implementing his Continental System.

events.title: Union forces win the Battle of Brown's Ferry near Chattanooga
events.description: Union forces led by General William Farrar Smith defeated Confederate forces at Brown's Ferry in Hamilton County, Tennessee, opening a supply line to the besieged city of Chattanooga.
events.html: Union forces led by General William Farrar Smith defeated Confederate forces at Brown's Ferry in Hamilton County, Tennessee, opening a supply line to the besieged city of Chattanooga.

events.title: The New York City Subway opens
events.description: The Interborough Rapid Transit Company opened New York's first underground line, from City Hall to 145th Street. Around 150,000 people rode on the first day of a network that grew into one of the world's largest.
